title: Extension by zero preserves products and derived limits
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$
be a quasi-compact open immersion with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$
and $B$ a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Then:

1. for every $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},j^*B)$ there is a distinguished
triangle, functorial in $K$,
$$
j_!K\longrightarrow Rj_*K\longrightarrow i_*i^*Rj_*K\longrightarrow j_!K[1];
$$
2. $j_!:D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},j^*B)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$ preserves
products and derived inverse limits $R\varprojlim$ of sequences;
3. on module sheaves, $j_!$ preserves products.

The coefficients on $U$ and $Z$ are the inverse images $j^*B$ and $i^*B$. The exact sheaf functors $j_!,i^*,i_*$ also denote their termwise induced functors on unbounded derived categories [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; $Rj_*$ is total right derived direct image [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Products are small products [def-weil-category-product], and a sequential derived limit means an object with a distinguished Roos triangle as in [def-weil-derived-limit].

external.place: *(2) Products and derived limits.* The pro-étale topos is replete, so products of sheaves are exact (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 3.1.10); hence the product in $D(-_{\mathrm{proét}})$ of a family of complexes is represented by the termwise product.

*(2) Products and derived limits.* The pro-étale topos is replete, so products of sheaves are exact (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 3.1.10); hence the product in $D(-_{\mathrm{proét}})$ of a family of complexes is represented by the termwise product.

proof.text: Use the universe and small-site convention [def-weil-size-convention]. For each of $X,U,Z$ the module category for the indicated ring sheaf is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]; no commutativity or constancy of $B$ is required. Hence [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] supplies K-injective representatives. Choose one $J$ for $K$ on $U$. The computation clause of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] identifies $Rj_*K$ with $j_*J$. The sheaf functors $j_!,j^*,i_*$ are exact by [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf], and $i^*$ is exact by [det-sf-open-closed-pullback-limits]. Applying [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to these exact functors permits termwise computation on every representative and makes their induced derived functors triangulated.

Apply clause (3) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] in every degree to $M=j_*J^q$. For an object $V\to U$, restriction and direct image give $(j^*j_*N)(V)=N(V\times_XU)=N(V)$; the maps and the coefficient actions are the identity under $V\times_XU=V$. Thus $j^*j_*J=J$ naturally, and the sequences assemble into $0\to j_!J\to j_*J\to i_*i^*j_*J\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] this produces a distinguished triangle natural in $J$. Step 1 identifies its objects with the three displayed terms of clause (1). Naturality passes from complexes to the derived category: compute morphisms on K-injective representatives, where the localization is fully faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; chain homotopies stay chain homotopies under the additive functors. The connecting map is the natural short-exact-sequence boundary, so this proves clause (1), including functoriality.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective); proetale.tex Tag 09BN (lemma-open-immersion); blueprint proof (1)

proof.text: For a $j^*B$-module sheaf $N$, apply the sheaf sequence of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] to $j_*N$ and the identity $j^*j_*N=N$ just verified. It identifies $j_!N$ with $\ker(j_*N\to i_*i^*j_*N)$. Products of module sheaves are computed sectionwise: coordinatewise restrictions and module actions make $V\mapsto\prod_\alpha N_\alpha(V)$ a sheaf, since a compatible family glues uniquely in each coordinate; maps into it are exactly families of maps into its factors. Consequently $j_*$ preserves products directly from $(j_*N)(W)=N(W\times_XU)$. Also $i_*$ preserves products: the adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$ named in [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(M,i_*\prod G_\alpha)=\operatorname{Hom}(i^*M,\prod G_\alpha)=\prod\operatorname{Hom}(M,i_*G_\alpha)$. By [det-sf-open-closed-pullback-limits], $i^*$ preserves products. The unit map $j_*N\to i_*i^*j_*N$ commutes with projections by naturality, so the two product identifications carry it to the product of the individual unit maps. Finally the kernel of a product map is the product of the kernels, section by section. This proves that the canonical comparison $j_!(\prod N_\alpha)\to\prod j_!N_\alpha$ is an isomorphism, including the empty product, and proves clause (3).

source.place: (2) Products and derived limits; sheaf-level kernel calculation making (3) explicit

proof.text: For a small family $(K_\alpha)$ on $U$, choose complex representatives $(C_\alpha)$. Apply [det-pe-products-derived] on $U$ with the ring sheaf $j^*B$, and on $X$ with $B$. The products in both derived categories are represented by the termwise products of these complexes. Exactness and termwise computation of $j_!$ were established in Step 1. The sheaf comparison of Step 3, in each degree, is a chain isomorphism $j_!(\prod C_\alpha)\cong\prod j_!C_\alpha$, since its construction is natural in the differentials. Its image in the localization is the canonical derived product comparison, as can be checked by composing with every projection. Hence $j_!$ preserves all small derived products.

source.place: (2) Products and derived limits, termwise-products argument

proof.text:
Let $(K_n,t_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n)$ be any inverse sequence in $D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},j^*B)$, and put $P=\prod_nK_n$, with $s$ characterized by $\mathrm{pr}_ns=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. Products exist by Step 4 and [det-pe-products-derived], and [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] therefore supplies a derived limit. Take any of its Roos triangles $L\to P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\to L[1]$ as in [def-weil-derived-limit]. Write $F=j_!$ and let $\phi:F(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}P'=\prod_nF(K_n)$ be the canonical isomorphism from Step 4. If $s'$ is the shift on $P'$ with transitions $F(t_n)$, then for each $n$,
$$\mathrm{pr}'_n\phi F(s)=F(\mathrm{pr}_ns)=F(t_n)F(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})=\mathrm{pr}'_ns'\phi.$$
The universal property of the product implies $\phi F(s)=s'\phi$, and additivity implies $\phi F(1-s)=(1-s')\phi$. Since $F$ is triangulated by Step 1 and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], applying it to the chosen triangle and using $\phi$ on the middle two terms yields the distinguished triangle $F(L)\to P'\xrightarrow{1-s'}P'\to F(L)[1]$. This is exactly the defining property [def-weil-derived-limit] of a derived limit of the image sequence. Thus $j_!$ preserves sequential derived limits, completing clause (2). If a separate Roos limit of the image sequence has been chosen, clause (1) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] identifies it with $F(L)$ up to isomorphism; no canonical choice of a cone in a bare triangulated category is being assumed.

split_report.summary: Rebuilt the earlier attempt after checking all cited statements. Added existing general Grothendieck/K-injective, natural complex-SES triangle and exact-derived-functor tools. Proved sheaf products by a kernel calculation, derived products termwise, and derived-limit preservation by an explicit projection calculation on the Roos triangle. Removed the inapplicable adic-coefficient exact-functor/Rlim citation and placeholder quotes. No new nodes. Second reader: cited the existing universe convention explicitly and independently repeated semantic, type-pattern and source searches; retained all five mathematical steps.

Step 3 proves proof (3) directly using the exact sheaf sequence, Step 4 realizes the product part of (2), and Step 5 realizes the Roos-fibre part of (2). The unit and chapter route are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Generic Grothendieck property for modules over arbitrary ring sheaves; the closed-unit unit supplies no such foundation.
Generic K-injective existence needed to compute unbounded Rj_*; not an alternative to any closed-unit argument.
Generic full faithfulness of K-injective representatives, needed for derived naturality.
The blueprint explicitly requires product preservation of closed inverse image for arbitrary ring-sheaf coefficients.
Generic termwise representation of derived products over an arbitrary pro-etale ring sheaf; this is the exact product input in the blueprint.
Generic existence and uniqueness up to isomorphism of a Roos limit once the product exists; no adic hypotheses or tower-category coefficient identification.
